answer: At the dawn of each validation cycle, the network requires every agent to generate a hardware-rooted attestation quote from an isolated enclave thread. This cryptographic signal binds the agent's identity to a signed hardware measurement. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of procuring physical enclave-capable processors per fake identity. However, microarchitectural side-channel leaks can expose private attestation keys, enabling adversaries to forge proofs on commodity machines.
